title: Influence Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC I
raw_text:
12.     MOS 1795, Influence Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. The Influence Chief is the Senior Staff Non-Commissioned
Officer that directly assists Influence Officers, Civil-Military Operations
Planners, and mentors and advises Influence Specialists. They manage the
conduct of influence operations and can facilitate the integration of
influences operations with other information activities and force maneuver in
the information environment. The Influence Chief assists in the planning,
training, deployment, and implementation of capabilities and resources
required to conduct influence operations. Influence Chiefs possess knowledge
on the joint operational and marine corps planning processes (JOPP/MCPP) in
order to develop integrated influence plans and operations.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess MOS 1751.

            (2) Attain promotion to MSgt.

        (3) Security requirement: must meet sensitive compartmented
information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background
investigation/T5 investigation.

    c. Requirements. For MOS and career progression, Staff Operations in
the Information Environment Planner Course (SOPC) (M02HE5D), Quantico, VA is
highly encouraged.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A CH1, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew
Members, All Other 55-3019.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Information Specialist, 0551.




                                          3-128                     Enclosure (1)
 3118                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



            (2) Civil Affairs Specialist, 1732.

            (3) Civil-Military Operations Chief, 1739.

            (4) Influence Specialist, 1751.
common_text: The Information Maneuver Occupational Field integrates information capability areas and the military occupational specialties (MOS) of cyberspace, space, electromagnetic warfare, civil affairs, and psychological operations into a single OCCFLD. Marines from these disciplines utilize their exquisite talents, knowledge, skills, and abilities to generate, preserve, and apply informational power against a relevant actor in order to increase or protect competitive advantage or combat power potential within all domains of the operating environment. Duty assignments include Marine Corps Forces Cyberspace Command, Marine Corps Forces Space Command, Marine Corps Information Command, Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion, Marine Corps Information Operations Center, MEF information groups, HQMC, MARFORs, joint organizations, and staff sections at all levels of the MAGTF.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
